summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 48% to ~INR9,543 crores and EBITDA 53% to ~INR559 crores, but Q4 EBITDA/ton fell to ~INR14,000 on formula and freight hits.
summary.overview: FY26 was the company's highest-ever year: consolidated revenue ~INR9,543 crores (+48%), EBITDA ~INR559 crores (+53%, margin 5.9%), PAT ~INR347 crores (+56%). Q4 FY26 was weak: revenue ~INR3,105 crores (+76% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell to ~3.5%, with copper EBITDA/ton compressed by sales-formula resets after a sharp LME rally and by Iran-related shipping and fuel costs. Management calls these temporary and says it has changed its buyer formula structure. Copper anode production started in March 2026, with cathode, wire rod and bus bar lines scheduled over Q2 FY27 to Q2 FY27 (Sept 2026).

financial_highlights.change: Compressed QoQ; no prior-quarter figure stated

financial_highlights.metric: Return on equity / return on capital employed (Mar 2026)

segments.name: Copper and copper alloy products
segments.commentary: ~55% of FY26 revenue. Copper EBITDA/ton was ~INR42,000 in Q3 FY26 and ~INR14,000 in Q4 FY26; management guides a normalised ~INR30,000-33,000/ton on an annual average for the existing business.

segments.name: Lead and lead alloy ingots
segments.commentary: ~40% of FY26 revenue. Lead volume ~1.85 lakh tons in FY26; utilisation ~97-100% of installed capacity, with management saying lead has effectively peaked.

segments.name: Aluminium and aluminium-related products
segments.commentary: ~5% of FY26 revenue. Capacity utilisation ~35% of installed capacity for FY26.

guidance_outlook: Normalised copper EBITDA guided at ~INR30,000-33,000/ton on a yearly average for the existing business, excluding value-added products; quarterly swings of INR30,000-37,000 expected.
Lead and copper volume growth guided at double digits; lead ~10-15%, copper could exceed 15%.
Value-added copper products (anode, cathode, wire rod, bus bar, profiles) seen adding ~INR25-45/kg EBITDA at current copper prices; conservative range INR22-45/kg.
Copper downstream projects expected to lift overall EBITDA margin by 2-4 percentage points (per management).
Working capital cycle targeted below 60 days from 66 days; operating cash flow expected positive from Q2 FY27 if achieved.
Management expects Q1 FY27 to show partial recovery as the ~INR6,000/ton war-related cost impact eases; formula impact expected to normalise.
Capex for FY27 around INR115-120 crores including antimony (~INR20 crores), plastic recycling (~INR15 crores), Ahmedabad JV (~INR30 crores), Kuwait (~INR30 crores) and copper phase two.
capex_capacity: Copper anode: first furnace of 800 MT/month started March 2026; second furnace (800 MT/month) due Q1 FY27, taking total to 1,600 MT/month.

Copper cathode: civil work complete, machinery erection under way; phase one commissioning by Q2 FY27 and phase two by Q3 FY27, reaching 1,500 MT/month. Imported machinery delayed by Iran shipping disruption.
Copper wire rod: 600 MT/month; machinery erection from June 2026, commissioning by August 2026.
Copper bus bar and profiles: 1,500 MT/month; machinery erection from July 2026, commissioning targeted September 2026.
Ahmedabad JV (Jain C&Y Circular Solution): premises leased; e-motor and cable scrap processing from September 2026; machinery installation by December 2026.
Kuwait battery recycling venture: civil work complete, machinery ready at supplier but shipment delayed; supplier ready on 30-day notice once routes normalise.
Standalone plastic recycling plant on ~6 acres, ~INR15 crores capex, operational by Q3 FY27; handles by-product plastic only.
Copper capacity utilisation ~65% of installed capacity in FY26, expected to rise over 2-3 years as new capacity is added.
demand_pricing: FY26 volume growth ~26.5%; the rest of revenue growth came from realisation.

Q4 volume fell QoQ across copper, lead and aluminium because containers were stuck at UAE ports (Jebel Ali transshipment) amid Hormuz disruption; management says new shipments now bypass Middle East ports.

Copper sales formulas moved sharply after LME rose ~40% (from ~US$10,000 to ~US$14,000/t). Management says formulas historically moved only 0.25-0.5%, and the company now plans long-term hedged formula contracts with buyers.
Q4 copper EBITDA/ton hit by ~INR6,000 from war-related freight, fuel and port costs and ~INR18,000-18,500 from higher LME and formula drop.
Export share 62% and domestic 38% of FY26 revenue.
Management says a 1% formula change moves copper EBITDA by ~INR13/kg; company buys ~80% of LME and sells ~98-99%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised copper EBITDA per ton once formula effects are stripped out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided ~INR30,000-33,000/ton on an annual average for the existing business, with quarters ranging ~INR30,000-37,000. Value-added products are excluded from this figure.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material is stuck at Middle East ports, and is it hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a percentage and offered to email container count and value. It said the stuck material is fully hedged, hedges roll over automatically every three months, and new shipments bypass the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: Is the copper and lead volume growth guidance higher than 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead growth guided at 10-15%; copper could be higher given rising scrap availability and applications, with management later saying it could exceed 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental EBITDA/kg will value-added copper products deliver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR25-45/kg at current copper prices, conservatively INR22-45/kg, on top of the ~INR32/kg base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow turn strongly negative (~INR600 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said higher copper prices and ~26% volume growth raised working capital; no fresh bank borrowing was taken, and receivables rose partly because discounted receivables are now shown gross under NFRA/Companies Act requirements.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other manufacturing/other expenses fall sharply in Q4 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the change reflects fair-value hedge M2M movements that were positive in the period. A detailed breakup will be sent by email.

risks_watch: Copper formula volatility: a 1% move in formula is ~INR13/kg EBITDA; management's long-term hedged formula change is not yet proven.
Stuck containers at UAE/Middle East ports and Hormuz disruption: value not disclosed; war charges possible.
Kuwait and cathode project delays from shipping disruption; Ahmedabad JV and other projects already slipped 2-3 months.
Operating cash flow of ~INR-600 crores and receivables build; working cycle target below 60 days is unconfirmed.
Q1 FY27 copper EBITDA/ton recovery is not yet confirmed; freight rates and copper prices remained high in April-May per analyst.
Hedging cost and mark-to-market effects on other expenses need clarity.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on the outlook, but defensive and sometimes evasive on specifics: formula mechanics, stuck-container value and copper EBITDA normalisation were deferred to follow-up emails. Management attributes Q4 weakness to one-time external factors.
key_quotes: The quarter four FY '26 result is not considered representative of the business underlying earning capacity.
Copper anode production has already commenced in March 2026 with an initial installed capacity of 800 metric ton per month.
We remain confident that the Q4 margin compression was a transient and not structural in nature.
This has been one-time impact and I'm sure it will not get repeated because of the tailwind goes up or down.
